outline.description: This chapter introduces the parties, the factual context of the dispute, and the sequence of events leading from the initial FOIA request to the appellate review.
subtopics: Foad Farahi's background and the nature of the FBI's interest in him
The FOIA request and the FBI's initial withholding of records
The initial summary judgment motion and the district court's requirement for updated declarations
The roles of the Hardy and Bender declarations
The district court's final grant of summary judgment in favor of the FBI

outline.chapter_title: The Legal Framework of FOIA Exemption 7(A)
outline.description: This chapter explains the statutory and judicial standards used to determine when law enforcement records can be withheld from public disclosure.
subtopics: Statutory language of 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(7)(A)
The 'compiled for law enforcement purposes' requirement
The 'pending or reasonably anticipated' standard for enforcement proceedings
The government's burden of proof in FOIA litigation
The doctrine of agency deference, specifically regarding national security and counterterrorism

outline.description: This chapter details how the court applied the legal standards of Exemption 7(A) to the specific facts of the case to determine if the FBI's withholdings were justified.
subtopics: Establishing the rational nexus between the records and law enforcement duties
Evaluating the 'ongoing' nature of the investigation through the Hardy and Bender declarations
Addressing the challenge to the 'terse' nature of updated declarations
The impact of the investigation's breadth on the plausibility of its continued pendency
The court's treatment of the plaintiff's forfeited arguments regarding document categories

outline.chapter_title: Segregability and the Use of Ex Parte Evidence
outline.description: This chapter examines the agency's obligation to release non-exempt information and the court's methodology for reviewing evidence that cannot be made public.
subtopics: The 'reasonably segregable' standard under § 552(a)(8)(A)(ii)
The 'inextricably intertwined' doctrine for withholding entire documents
The distinction between disclosing 'meaningful information' versus individual words or phrases
The legal validity of relying on ex parte declarations in national security contexts
The balance between the plaintiff's right to review and the need for government secrecy

outline.description: This chapter summarizes the court's final ruling and the legal significance of the outcome.
subtopics: Summary of the DC Circuit's findings on Exemption 7(A) and segregability
The final holding and the affirmation of the district court's judgment
